**Daily Macro Digest — 7 August 2026**

**Summary:** It was a mixed, moderately volatile session. Oil jumped hard (WTI +3.8%) even as one headline flagged a possible easing of Middle East ("Hormuz") tensions — a genuine contradiction in the newsflow that's worth flagging rather than smoothing over. Gold rose 1.1% while silver slipped nearly 1%, a classic "fear" divergence (gold/silver ratio rising) even though the VIX (volatility index, a "fear gauge") actually fell 4%, and equities markets look calm. The US dollar and 10-year Treasury yield both firmed, AUD/USD eased slightly, and ASX materials names were roughly flat-to-down. No asset here crossed the "unusual move" threshold today (none flagged as anomalies) — even oil's near-4% jump sits within its normal range historically, so no historical-pattern comparisons apply.
